findings.title: website_name leaks a profile website hidden from anonymous viewers
findings.body: `website_name` is derived from `object.user_profile.website`, but it is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list, which hides `:website` when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` is true for TL0 users viewed anonymously, and it has no other scope check. An anonymous viewer can still receive the website host and path through `website_name` even though `website` itself is suppressed. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or apply the same restriction in its include method.

findings.title: `include_website_name` is not recognized as an inclusion guard
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults methods named `include_<attribute>?`; a method named `include_website_name` without the trailing question mark is ignored. Consequently `website_name` is always serialized when the attribute exists (and `website_name: null` is emitted for users without a website), and the intended `website.present?` guard is dead code. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Test coverage misses website_name restriction for anonymous TL0 users
findings.body: The TL0/anonymous test only checks the existing untrusted attribute list and never sets a website, while the new website_name tests use a normal viewer. There is no regression test proving `website_name` is omitted when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` hides the profile website, which is exactly the case where the new attribute currently leaks data.
